title: The Ten Plagues IQ
subtitle: Frogs, locusts, darkness. How much of the Exodus story do you really remember?

questions.text: What was the very first plague God sent on Egypt?

options.explanation: In Exodus 7:20 the water of the Nile turned to blood, and that was plague number one.
Frogs came next, as the second plague, after the river turned to blood.
Darkness was the ninth plague, near the very end.
Locusts were the eighth plague, long after the first.

questions.text: Who did God send to confront Pharaoh and demand that Israel be let go?

options.explanation: Joshua led Israel much later, after Moses died, not during the plagues.
God sent Moses, and Aaron went with him as his spokesman before Pharaoh (Exodus 4:14-16).
Abraham lived generations earlier and never set foot in Pharaoh's court during the Exodus.
Joseph rose to power in Egypt long before, but he was not part of the plagues.

questions.text: What happened when Aaron threw down his rod before Pharaoh?

options.explanation: Aaron's rod budded later in the wilderness (Numbers 17), not here in Pharaoh's court.
Exodus 7:10 says the rod became a serpent, and it swallowed up the serpents of Pharaoh's magicians.
The ground swallowing rebels happens later with Korah, not with Aaron's rod here.
The rod did not burn. It turned into a serpent.

questions.text: Which plague brought painful boils on the people and the animals?

options.explanation: Hail was a different plague that struck down crops and livestock left in the fields.
Flies filled the houses, but they did not cause the boils.
Exodus 9:9-10 describes ashes thrown toward heaven that became boils breaking out on man and beast.
Lice came earlier and covered man and beast, but they were not boils.

questions.text: During the plague of darkness, what did the Israelites have in their homes?

options.text: Nothing different, they sat in the dark too
options.explanation: The darkness did not touch them the way it touched Egypt.
Exodus 10:23 says the Egyptians sat in thick darkness, but the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

options.text: Pillars of fire in every house
options.explanation: The pillar of fire guided Israel later in the wilderness, not during this plague.

options.text: Lamps given to them by Pharaoh
options.explanation: Pharaoh gave them nothing. The light in their homes came from God.

questions.text: What was the final and most severe plague?

options.explanation: Exodus 12:29 records that the firstborn of Egypt died at midnight, from Pharaoh's son to the captive's son.
There was no earthquake among the ten plagues.
The Nile turned to blood as the first plague, but it did not dry up as the last.
Hail mixed with fire came earlier, but the final plague was the death of the firstborn.

questions.text: What did God tell Israel to put on their doorposts so the destroyer would pass over them?

options.explanation: The sign on the doors was blood, not oil.
Exodus 12:7 told them to strike the blood on the two side posts and the upper door post of their houses.
Ashes were used in the plague of boils, not on the doorposts.
They ate unleavened bread that night, but the sign on the door was the lamb's blood.

questions.text: What did the plague of frogs do to the land of Egypt?

options.text: The frogs ate all the crops
options.explanation: Locusts devoured the crops later. The frogs simply overran everything.

options.text: The frogs covered the land, even the houses and beds
options.explanation: Exodus 8:3-4 says the frogs went up into the houses, the bedchambers, and the kneading troughs.
The water was already struck in the first plague. The frogs came out of it, but did not poison it.

options.text: The frogs only stayed by the river
options.explanation: They did not stay by the river. They spread into homes and beds across Egypt.

questions.text: Whose magicians copied some of the early plagues with their secret arts?

options.explanation: Canaan was not part of this story. The magicians served Pharaoh in Egypt.
Babylon comes much later in the Bible and had nothing to do with the plagues.
Exodus 7:11 says Pharaoh's wise men and sorcerers copied some signs, until they could not keep up with God.
Israel's elders followed Moses. They did not work against God's plagues.

questions.text: How did Pharaoh finally respond after the last plague?

options.explanation: In Exodus 12:31 Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron by night and told them to rise up and go.
Pharaoh did not arrest Moses. He sent the people away.
He could not ignore the death of his own firstborn. He finally relented.

options.text: He offered to share his throne
options.explanation: Pharaoh never offered his throne. He simply let the people leave.

questions.text: What lasting feast did God give Israel to remember this night of deliverance?

options.explanation: The Day of Atonement is a separate holy day about cleansing from sin, not the Exodus night.
Tabernacles recalls Israel living in booths in the wilderness, not the night of the firstborn.
Exodus 12:14 says this day would be a memorial, kept as a feast forever. We call it the Passover.
Pentecost came fifty days later and marked a different event in Israel's calendar.

scoring.perfectMessage: Perfect. You know the Exodus inside and out.
